content: 1. MMAE is metabolized by the enzyme CYP3A4. When polatuzumab vedotin is co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, the area under the curve (AUC) of unconjugated MMAE may increase, potentially leading to enhanced toxicities associated with polatuzumab vedotin. 2. Posaconazole can elevate the levels or effects of darunavir by interfering with hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring for increased adverse reactions to darunavir or cobicistat is recommended. 3. Darunavir reduces the effects of pramlintide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Reports suggest hyperglycemia may occur due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. 4. Darunavir increases pravastatin levels through an unknown mechanism, likely involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Similarly, cobicistat also increases pravastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating therapy adjustment and close monitoring. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 5. Both cobicistat and darunavir increase praziquantel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 6. Darunavir elevates prednisolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while prednisolone decreases darunavir levels through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Darunavir increases the levels of primaquine, progesterone (in various forms), and propafenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clinical monitoring is particularly advised when co-administering with antiarrhythmics. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels of protriptyline by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Careful dose titration of the antidepressant is recommended, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during co-administration with cobicistat. 9. Cobicistat and darunavir both increase quazepam and quetiapine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Quinidine levels are increased by cobicistat and darunavir through CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Quinidine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and P-gp and inhibits CYP2D6 and P-gp. Cobicistat, being a substrate and inhibitor of these enzymes, further amplifies this interaction. 11. Cobicistat and darunavir increase quinine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 12. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 13. Cobicistat and darunavir increase quizartinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. When co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day or interrupt its use. After discontinuing the strong inhibitor for 5 half-lives, resume the previous quizartinib dose. 14. Cobicistat increases rabeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Darunavir and cobicistat increase repaglinide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Cobicistat increases rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg orally every other day and monitor for associated adverse reactions like neutropenia and uveitis. Rifabutin decreases cobicistat levels through the same pathway. 17. Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Darunavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Cobicistat and darunavir increase ripretinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), raising the risk of adverse reactions. 20. Cobicistat increases risperidone levels by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be required during co-administration. 21. Darunavir increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Darunavir increases rivaroxaban levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with known combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Cobicistat increases roflumilast levels (both systemic and topical) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases roflumilast topical levels through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Cobicistat increases romidepsin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Darunavir increases ropivacaine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 26. Darunavir decreases rosiglitazone effects through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 27. Darunavir and cobicistat increase rosuvastatin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 28. Rucaparib increases cobicistat and darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 29. Rufinamide decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Cobicistat increases seladelpar levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Monitor seladelpar for adverse effects when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 31. Darunavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Cobicistat increases selexipag levels by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Selexipag is an ABCG2 (BCRP) substrate. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when co-administered with ABCG2 inhibitors. 33. Cobicistat increases selpercatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If co-administration is required, reduce the selpercatinib dose to 40 mg twice daily if the original dose was 120 mg twice daily, or to 80 mg twice daily if the original dose was 160 mg twice daily. 34. Darunavir increases sertraline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while decreasing sertraline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Dose titration of SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may be required to achieve the desired antidepressant effect. 35. Darunavir increases sildenafil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with PDE-5 inhibitors may increase the risk of associated adverse reactions, such as hypotension, syncope, visual disturbances, and priapism. 36. Cobicistat and darunavir increase sirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Darunavir decreases sitagliptin effects through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. 38. Darunavir increases solifenacin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Darunavir increases sorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Darunavir increases stiripentol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 41. Cobicistat increases sufentanil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of sufentanil with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 42. Darunavir increases sunitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Darunavir and cobicistat increase tacrolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 44. Tazemetostat decreases cobicistat and darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 45. Darunavir increases tasimelteon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 46. Tecovirimat decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer.
